messages.subject: error on installing R/QTL
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm installing R/QTL under windows directly from the zip file using  R
version 2.14.0. I get the following error message:

 Error in library(pkg, character.only = TRUE) :
 package ‘qtl’ does not have a NAMESPACE and should be re-installed

Is there any obvious reason (and fix) for this other than user
stupidity)?

Thanks,

Ian

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] error on installing R/QTL
messages.body_plain:
This isn't user stupidity.  R 2.14 is now requiring a NAMESPACE file within each package which previously had been just suggested.

I'm working on this and expect to release a new version that resolves the issue within the next week.

In the meantime, either stick with R 2.13.2 or install the package via install.packages().

karl

messages.subject: 'pseudo' backcross
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl

I have a cross between a clonal line and an outbred. Do you think it
would be valid to analyse it as  a backcross in R/qtl?

Thanks
messages.body_snippet:
Dear Karl

I have a cross between a clonal line and an outbred. Do you think it
would be valid to analyse it as  a backcross in R/qtl?

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] 'pseudo' backcross
messages.body_plain:
Provided that you know phase in the outbred parent, it has the same structure as a backcross, and so may be analyzed that way in R/qtl or any other software.

karl

messages.subject: marker regression data
messages.body_plain:
Karl and fellow Rqtl-ers,
I would like to do some marker regressions and I was wondering if there was any straightforward way of getting all of the regression statistics out from the analysis, and not just the LOD scores (slopes and intercepts).  I may just write a function to do all of the regressions, but I thought I would check to see if there would be any quick way to do it using scanone and method 'mr'.

Thanks,
Kevin
messages.body_snippet:

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] marker regression data
messages.body_plain:
No; at present, scanone only provides LOD scores.  Estimated effects can only be obtained through fitqtl.   The effectscan function might work, too.

karl

messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.22-21
messages.body_plain:
A new version of R/qtl (1.22-21) has been released at its web site
(http://www.rqtl.org).  It should be on CRAN within a couple of days.

There were quite a number of changes; see http://www.rqtl.org/STATUS.txt
for a complete list.  The major changes are below.

Karl Broman
kbr...@biostat.wisc.edu

------

Version 1.22, 11/28/2011:

Major changes:

  Revised plot.map to deal with a pair of maps with markers in
  different orders (or with some markers appearing in one map and not
  the other).  We still require that the two maps have the same
  chromosomes and chromosome names (with chromosomes in the same
  order).

  Revised scantwo to allow analysis of individual chromosome pairs,
  and reorganized the way that scantwo permutations are done (first
  summarizing each chromosome pair and then overall); this should
  eliminate the memory problems we've had with scantwo permutations.

messages.body_plain:
> The function works if i search for additive only and change the max.qtl =8.
> Though i have an extra question. If i run fitqtl (see code at the end)
> there are 6 df, although it ends up with 2 QTLs shouldn't be 2 df instead?

This is a four-way cross, and so each QTL has 3 degrees of freedom.
With two additive QTL, then overall there are 6 df.

That it is a four-way cross is likely the problem...the code is not as
well tested for this case, and the two maps need to be dealt with
specially.

karl

messages.body_plain:
What's happening is that you have just 24 individuals, and so you
can't fit these epistatic models.

The pLOD=208.8824 for QTL interacting with Q1 was suspicious, but the
real problem is that the LOD scores in step 3 are all NA, and the code
doesn't deal with that properly.

In the short term: focus on additive QTL.

In the longer term: I need to revise stepwiseqtl to handle those NAs.

karl
